Quick triage notes (initial, non-blocking):
- Timeline: deployment of quantized v2.3 model to the inference pool at ~08:27 UTC; KV cache warm-up anomalies recorded starting ~08:34 UTC.
- Symptom: increased host-side queueing and intermittent cache misalignment leading to OOM/retry behavior and 500s on the API layer.
- Evidence: attached trace_summary.json (sampled request traces showing cache misses spiking and repeated kernel restarts).

Immediate mitigations I propose (in order):
1) Roll back traffic to the previous v2.2 model (hotfix rollback). Estimated impact: ~3–7 minutes to cut and route traffic back, expected to drop error rate below 1% if model is the cause.
2) If rollback not possible: enable conservative prefix caching + reduce max_batch_size to lower mem pressure (config change that applies in ~2–4 minutes).
3) Provision 2x burst nodes from Dedicated pool as temporary breathing room (Aditya to confirm cost/availability).

ETA for first measurable improvement if we rollback now: 10–12 minutes. I'll stand by on the bridge and start the rollback immediately upon go.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-08-09T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update: latency/error surge — next steps and follow-up

Derek / Alice,

Thank you for your patience and for flagging the issue. Summary of what happened and where we are:

Summary:
- Root cause: regression tied to the v2.3 quantized model rollout which led to KV cache misalignment and memory pressure on a subset of inference hosts.
- Impact window: ~2027-08-08 08:30–09:20 UTC.
- Customer impact: elevated 95th percentile latency and ~12% 500s at peak; order ingestion delays observed.

Actions taken:
- We rolled back to v2.2 within 12 minutes of detection; telemetry indicates error rate dropped to <1% after rollback.
- Temporary Dedicated capacity was provisioned for the peak window and deprovisioned after stability confirmed.
- Postmortem in progress; root-cause remediation includes additional KV cache validation checks in rollout pipeline and stricter canary thresholds.

Customer-facing remediation and credits:
- We're prepared to issue a pro-rata credit for the impacted window (Marissa will follow up with a proposed calculation).
- We will schedule a live review with your engineering team to walk through traces and remediation steps.

Links & references:
- Incident page: https://redwood.status/incident/INC-20270808-pluto
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/PLUTO-7890

Next steps:
- Marissa will send the credit calculation and a short postmortem within 72 hours.
- Karthik's team will push rollout pipeline changes and increased canary traffic thresholds next week.

We appreciate the urgency and will keep you closely informed. Please reply if you'd like an immediate bridge for a detailed engineering walk-through.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
